newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Crude Outlook - bear market rally in near-term.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Crude Outlook - bear market rally in near-term.

text.p: U.S. crude prices are expected to remain strong early in the week in what analysts are calling a "bear market rally," though physical market fundamentals point to continued weakness.

With benchmark May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) futures hitting $18.96 support twice last week after a fall of nearly 30 percent since the start of the year, the market is targeting $20.40 to see whether the bounce is sustainable.

"The bias in the market is to reach modestly higher numbers," said William Brown, president of W.H. Brown & Co. in New York. For sustained gains the market must push above $20.40, where a convergence of chart factors, notably the 20-day moving average, would likely trigger fund and chart buying, Brown added.
Also contributing to the upward price momentum were tensions between Iran and the West.
The European Community and Iran have swapped diplomatic blows after a German court last week found Iranian involvement in the assassination of Kurdish dissidents.
Also, Sunday's Washington Post reported that U.S. and Saudi intelligence authorities have linked an Iranian government official to suspects in last year's bombing of a U.S. military compound.
Iran is the second-largest producer within the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, pumping about 3.7 million barrels a day, according to the latest Reuters survey.
However, traders cautioned that weekly inventory data could throw the market off any short-term firming trend, with continued signs of high crude imports likely to deflate technical momentum.

For the domestic crude grades, cash players said differentials were expected to remain relatively rangebound. Sweet grades gained strength last week after Shell was seen pulling back from offering Brent into the U.S. Gulf.
Once the fear of a Brent onslaught was removed, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James (LLS) saw differntials gain from 10-15 cts to hover around 30 cts below the May WTI marker.
Still, traders said there was plently of crude from overseas to pressure LLS and other sweet grades from gaining too much in the near-term.
"There is no shortage of offerings in the Gulf, Brent or no Brent. West African and Latin American barrels can be had," said a Texas cash trader.
Sour differentials were also stuck in a 10-15 cts trading belt, putting West Texas Sour/Midland around a $2.25 discount to the benchmark.
Traders said sour found support from improved margins and a stronger stance for Med Urals grades.
